Insurance help for Indiana residents

If you live in Indiana and you're sorting through Medicare, health, or life insurance, it's easy to feel buried — mailers, TV ads, and call centers all pulling in different directions. Honorbrook exists to cut through that. We're an independent agency, which means we work for you, not for one insurance company, and we'll walk you through your real options in plain English.

We help Hoosiers who are turning 65, already on Medicare and unsure their plan still fits, retiring or losing employer coverage, shopping for coverage under 65, or simply wanting a second opinion from someone who isn't paid to push one product. And our help is always free — carriers pay us a commission when we place a policy, so you never pay a fee, and by law your premium is identical whether you use us or enroll on your own.

Schedule a Medicare review

Booking opens Luay’s page on PlanEnroll. Create your profile there and ask for your meeting. Having these ready makes the first conversation useful:

  • Your Medicare card, or the dates your Part A and Part B start.
  • The doctors and hospitals you want to keep.
  • A list of your prescriptions and the pharmacy you use.
  • Whether you have Medicaid or get help paying Medicare costs.

When PlanEnroll asks what type of meeting you would like, choose Health. You may be asked to complete a short Scope of Appointment form first. It does not obligate you to enroll. The first open time is at least 24 hours ahead. To talk sooner, call (301) 615-8289 or text (571) 354-0146.

Coverage we offer in Indiana

  • Medicare Advantage — all-in-one Part C plans, with premiums, networks and benefits that vary by plan.
  • Medicare Supplement (Medigap) — see any doctor who accepts Medicare.
  • Part D drug plans — the total yearly cost for your medication list, compared.
  • final expense — cover funeral and end-of-life costs.
  • life insurance — term and whole life to protect your family.
  • ICHRA — reimbursement-based health coverage for employers and employees.
  • ACA plans (under 65) — Marketplace coverage with subsidy help.
  • group / SHOP coverage — small-business and team plans.

We also help with annuities, cancer and critical illness coverage, dental, vision and hearing coverage and hospital indemnity coverage.

Serving communities across Indiana

Wherever you are in the state, we can help. From the Indianapolis metro to the smaller towns along the back roads, Honorbrook serves Hoosiers in every county — including Indianapolis, Fort Wayne, Evansville, South Bend, Carmel, Fishers, and Bloomington. Everything is handled by phone, so there's no office visit and no driving across town — just a friendly conversation when it works for you.

Free local Medicare counseling in Indiana — and how we fit in

Where Honorbrook adds value is the next step: comparing the specific Medicare Advantage, Medigap, and Part D plans offered in your county, checking that your doctors and prescriptions are covered, and helping you enroll and stay on track year after year.

We help residents in and around Indianapolis, Fort Wayne, Evansville, and South Bend, as well as smaller communities across Indiana. Because plans and networks differ from one county to the next, we always start with your ZIP code.

Plan availability varies by county in Indiana — the Medicare Advantage, Medigap, and drug plans offered in Marion County aren't always the same as those in Allen or Vanderburgh County. We check what's actually available at your exact address so you only compare plans you can really enroll in.

Common questions

Indiana Medicare & insurance FAQ

Do you charge Indiana residents for help?
No — our help is completely free. Carriers pay us a commission when we place a policy, and by law your premium is identical whether you use an agent or enroll on your own. You get our guidance at no added cost.
Which Indiana cities do you serve?
All of Indiana, handled by phone — including Indianapolis, Fort Wayne, Evansville, South Bend, Carmel, Fishers, and Bloomington, plus every community in between. No office visit needed.
What plans can I get in Indiana?
Availability varies by county. We compare the Medicare Advantage, Medigap, Part D, ACA, ICHRA, and life options actually offered at your exact address, so you only look at plans you can really enroll in.
Can you help if I'm new to Indiana or moving?
Yes. A move — including into or within Indiana — can open a Special Enrollment Period that lets you change or pick up coverage outside the usual windows. We'll check your timing and the plans available at your new home.
